WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"This is Ahasuerus which reigned, from India even unto Ethiopia, over an hundred and seven and twenty provinces." Esther 1:1
He "set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti". Esther 2:17

He gave his ring to Haman to seal the decree against the Jews, and later to Mordecai: "the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse". Esther 3:10–12 Esther 8:2 Esther 8:8
"And the king Ahasuerus laid a tribute upon the land, and upon the isles of the sea." His acts are "written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia". Esther 10:1–2
Ezra: "in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, wrote they unto him an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem." Ezra 4:6
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Purim was confirmed by letters "to the hundred twenty and seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus". Esther 9:30–32
Judah's enemies wrote to him against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem. Ezra 4:6
He sealed Haman's decree to destroy the Jews, then a second decree letting them defend themselves. Esther 3:13 Esther 8:11
"Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews." Esther 10:3

SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Third, seventh and twelfth years named; no length of reign.
IF XERXES I: DECEMBER 486 – 465 BC (PARKER AND DUBBERSTEIN, 1942)

On this identification his third year was 483/482, his seventh 479/478 and his twelfth 474/473 BC. An Elephantine papyrus dated "year 21", when "King Artaxerxes sat on his throne", shows Xerxes' reign had ended by early 464 BC.
IF XERXES I: 485–465 BC (EASTON, 1915)
The older reckoning in the 1915 encyclopedia.
Darius I, son of Hystaspes
James Ussher (1658)

Ussher identified Ahasuerus with Darius, Vashti with Atossa and Esther with Artystone, Darius's wives in Herodotus; he saw the tribute "upon the isles of the sea" (Esth 10:1) as fitting Darius, who first laid a fixed tribute on his subjects. Esther 10:1 [25][8]
Xerxes I
the Jewish Encyclopedia (1901), listing Keil, Bertheau, Ryssel, Wildeboer, Sayce and Schrader; R. Dick Wilson (1915)

The Hebrew name is the Persian Khshayarsha, which the Greeks wrote Xerxes. The Jewish Encyclopedia adds that between his third and seventh years Ahasuerus "is lost to view" in Esther, the years when Xerxes invaded Greece. Esther 1:3 Esther 2:16 [22][11]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say how long Ahasuerus reigned or how he died.
Esther gives no verdict on him, and no prophet is named in his reign.
The book of Esther, as the KJV translates the Hebrew, never uses the name God or LORD (our search of the text).
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textThis page covers the Ahasuerus of Esther and of Ezra 4:6; whether they are the same king is a question below. The Ahasuerus of Daniel 9:1, father of Darius the Mede, is a different man with his own record. Esther 1:1 Ezra 4:6 Daniel 9:1
Scholars' viewMost scholars since the 19th century identify him with Xerxes I (486–465 BC): "Ahasuerus" renders the Persian name Khshayarsha, which the Greeks wrote Xerxes.[22][11][14]
